gold_comments.evidence_requirement: The added code still uses role_field='workflow_admin_role', 'use_role', and 'read_role' in check_related calls, and produces role-specific error messages, contradicting the reviewer's instruction to use a generic 403 and DAB RBAC principles.

gold_comments._reviewer_comment_full:
This isn't true any more. `workflow_admin_role` is a role. The core idea of the new system (DAB RBAC) is that it enumerates permissions of a role. So access control only considers permissions, never roles. You get permissions from roles, but policy evaluators should never know what role gave you the permission.

I also don't think that we need this, and I would say it would be more _consistent_ right now to give an unqualified 403 "you do not have permission to perform this action" error message, considering that it was the "add" permission lacked for the "add" action.
